description: Agent triggers on REVIEW routing. Adapted from the plan's original design (trigger on low self-confidence, e.g. 0.35) - T026 found self-confidence unusable (AUROC 0.554), so the real trigger is rule-baseline disagreement (T027). Real case: RAG predicted Entailment, the agent was invoked and investigated.
Agent does NOT trigger when the rule baseline agrees with RAG. Real case: RAG predicted NotMentioned, rule baseline agreed - routed ACCEPT, agent never invoked (pipeline/confidence.py's route()).

Agent picks a relevant tool. Real trace: ['find_defined_term', 'fallback_classify'] - called find_defined_term for a hypothesis referencing a term that's likely defined elsewhere in the document (nda-2, about a specific defined-term scope limitation).

Agent stops after finding clear evidence, not the max step budget. Real case: concluded in 1 step(s) (cap is 5). Across all 67 real REVIEW cases, 52/67 concluded normally and none reached the 5-step cap - the model typically decides quickly rather than over-investigating.

Agent detects a query loop. Real trace: ['search_clauses', 'search_clauses', 'fallback_classify'] - the model repeated the same tool+query combination, tripping duplicate-call detection (pipeline/agent.py) before hitting the step cap. 14/67 real cases (21%) hit this - the single most common non-'concluded' stop reason.
Agent improves on RAG. Real case: RAG predicted NotMentioned, agent corrected it to Entailment (gold: Entailment). 6/67 real REVIEW cases (9.0%) show this pattern.

Agent makes it worse - CRITICAL FAILURE. Real case: RAG correctly predicted Entailment (matches gold Entailment), agent flipped it to Contradiction (wrong). 3/67 real REVIEW cases (4.5%) show this pattern - real, tracked, and outweighed by recovery (9.0%) but not zero. This is the number T031's architecture decision should weigh, not just the net accuracy gain.
